advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the duplicated Cloud credential guards: apply the same strip()/email rules (or delegate) in `assert_env_ready` and `_build_jira_backend` so both paths enforce identical checks and messages.
evidence: backend.py:183-208 `def assert_env_ready` collects missing among JIRA_URL/JIRA_USER/JIRA_API_TOKEN with `if not value` (no `.strip()`, no email check)
backend.py:300 factory uses `if not (value or "").strip()` and backend.py:320-321 adds the email `partition('@')` check

_attestation.py:67-68 `backend = select_backend(load_config())` (constructs via `_build_jira_backend`) precedes `backend.assert_env_ready()`, so the factory guard preempts assert_env_ready on that path
test_backend_scalar_surface_heldout.py:76 exercises `assert_env_ready()` directly with `user='u@x'` — that path never gets the factory's whitespace/email rules
advisory.finding: The new construction-time guard in `_build_jira_backend` and the pre-existing `JiraBackend.assert_env_ready` (backend.py:183-208) now check the same three vars with DIVERGENT rules: the factory uses `(value or '').strip()` (rejects whitespace-only) plus an email-format check, while `assert_env_ready` uses `not value` (accepts whitespace-only) and has NO email check, and emits a different message. On the attestation path the factory runs first and shadows `assert_env_ready`, but a direct `assert_env_ready()` call still accepts a whitespace-only or non-email JIRA_USER — an inconsistent credential contract.
scenarios: A caller invoking backend.assert_env_ready() directly with a whitespace-only or non-email JIRA_USER gets no failure, unlike the factory path.
Future edits to assert_env_ready's message/rules drift silently because it is unreachable on the normal attestation path and only the factory message is asserted by the new tests.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extract the presence+email check into one helper and call it from both `_build_jira_backend` and `JiraBackend.assert_env_ready`, so whitespace-only rejection and the email-format check apply on both paths and there is a single message.
